Briefly stating in the present case, land situated within the revenue estate of village Basant Pura,
Tehsil Radaur, District Yamuna Nagar at Jagadhari (the then Kurukshetra) belonging to the appellant- landowners came to be acquired vide notification dated 31.12.1981 issued under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) followed by notification dated 09.02.1982 issued under Section 6 thereof.
Award under Section 11 of the Act was passed by Land Acquisition Collector on 10.08.1998.
The purpose of acquisition was for construction of road from Radaur to Khera Lakha Singh and the total land acquired for the said purpose was 7.26 acres.

4. Aggrieved of the award passed by the Land Acquisition Collector, the appellants-landowners filed Reference Petition under Section 18 of the Act seeking the market value at the rate of 1,00,000/-
per acre.

The parties having led their respective evidence, the Reference Court vide its award dated 10.08.1998 dismissed the claims filed at the instance of appellants-landowners, against which the present appeals came to be filed 5.

Impugning the aforementioned award, learned counsel for the appellants-landowners submits that the Reference Court went wrong while discarding the sale deed Ex. P-1 produced by the appellants-landowners whereby, 5 marlas of land was sold for a sum of Rs.6,000/- and the value of one acre would come to around Rs.1,92,000/-.

He further submits that the said sale deed was required to be considered by the Reference Court while applying an appropriate RFA-302-1999,
RFA-825-1999, RFA- 998-1999 and RFA- 999-1999 cut thereupon, while determining the amount of compensation.

He also submits that considering the fact that the land under acquisition was abutting the already existing road, whereas, land forming part of sale deed Ex.P1 being at some distance therefrom, would pale into insignificance as the notification was issued after a gap of more than two years thereafter.

6. On the other hand, learning state counsel opposes the prayer made here in while submitting that the impugned award warrants no interference as the sale deed Ex.P1, which pertains to 5 marlas was rightly discarded being related to a small piece of land.

He further submits that sale deed Ex.P1 could not have been considered by the Reference Court, the same being post notification under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act 1984 with a gap of more than two years.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the book.
I find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-landowners.

8. At the time of hearing, for assistance of this Court, Aks shajra pertaining to village Basantpura,
Tehsil Radaur, District Yamuna Nagar has been produced by the learned State counsel which was not disputed by learned counsel for the appellants.

Having gone through the same with the assistance of revenue officials present in Court, it has been found that the land forming part of sale deed Ex. P1 is situated at a distance of mere 260 meter from the land under acquisition which cannot be termed to be too far off.

In such circumstances, the Reference Court could not have Hazoor Singh & Ors vs State Of Haryana on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133729019/
2 rejected the consideration of sale deed RFA-302-1999, RFA-825-1999, RFA- 998-1999 and RFA- 999-1999 Ex. P1 in toto, but rather could have relied upon the same after having applied some appropriate cut towards the development of the land while considering the land forming part thereof to be small.

sentences.text: In the given facts, the land under acquisition was already abutting the existing road leading from Village Radaur to Khera Lakha Singh which further connects Ambala and District Yamuna Nagar and the acquisition in hand was merely for widening thereof

, as such it was having better locational and potential value as compared to the land forming part of the sale deed Ex.P-1.
9.

In view of the given facts and circumstances, the sale deed Ex.P1 could have been considered for the purpose of determination of compensation upon applying a cut of 75% thereon, by determining the compensation at the uniform rate of 48,000/- per acre along with all other statutory benefits and interest thereupon.
10. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed in the aforesaid terms and the award dated 10.08.1998 passed by the Reference Court- cum-Additional District Judge, Jagadhari is hereby modified.
